reliability depends on the ROI and the task.

reliability in developmental fMRI studies depends on a multitude of factors and that the reliability of different ROIs and tasks should be investigated in each study separately to ensure a valid interpretation of the findings.
the reliability of fMRI data in adolescents depends on the type and location of ROI.

the emotional attention task was more reliable in terms of ICC, while the cognitive control task was more reliable when looking at variability in terms of SD.

longitudinal studies should consider the task and ROI when interpreting their results and when choosing their study sample size.

the reliability of fMRI data is not only influenced by the task but also by the ROI.
